episodes.title: Morning Drop-Off Window
episodes.text: You arrive behind the pharmacy counter and open the refill stack. You pick up a written prescription and check the name, drug, and dose line by line. One line looks blank.

trial.title: Find the missing piece
trial.scenario: You hold a refill request for a regular patient. The drug name is there but the dose and doctor signature are missing.
options: Enter it anyway and fix it later
Hold it for verification before entering
File it in the finished stack
trial.explain: You cannot enter a prescription until the missing information is complete and verified.

episodes.title: Typing Into System
episodes.text: You sit down at the computer with the verified prescriptions. You type the patient name, drug, and directions into the database. You double-check each field as you go.

choice.prompt: The handwriting on the strength is hard to read. What do you do?

options.label: Type your best guess to keep the line moving
options.outcome: The entry saves, but the wrong strength stays in the system until someone catches it.

options.label: Stop and verify the strength before typing
options.outcome: The line pauses while you check the original request and confirm the correct strength.

episodes.title: Same Typing Again
episodes.text: You sit back down with the next batch of verified slips. You type names, drugs, and directions into the same database. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Updating Patient Lists
episodes.text: You pull up a patient profile on the screen. You add the new medication to the list they already take. You save the updated profile for the next refill.

episodes.title: Rejected Insurance Claim
episodes.text: You open the insurance claim that came back rejected. The pharmacist waits while you sort out the form.

choice.prompt: The claim form has a wrong code and is missing a date. What do you do first?

options.label: Correct the code and add the missing date, then resubmit
options.outcome: You update the form and send it back. It goes into the queue for processing again.

options.label: Resubmit the same form as-is
options.outcome: The form sends again with the same error and comes back rejected.

options.label: Set the form aside and move to the next one
options.outcome: The claim stays unpaid and the record stays open on your desk.

chat.text: This claim bounced back. Can you check the form?
See if the patient info or code is off and fix it for resubmit.

episodes.title: Adding Up Charges
episodes.text: You sit with the list of medications dispensed to hospital patients. You compute each charge and type the amounts into the computer. You save the entries and close the file.

episodes.title: Morning Tray Check
episodes.text: You arrive before the first patient. You pull out the blood-drawing tray and wipe it down. You check each packet to make sure needles and syringes are sealed and first-time use.

trial.title: Check the tray
trial.scenario: You look over the tray for the morning draw. One syringe wrapper is torn open and the needle sits loose. The rest of the instruments look sterile and sealed.
options: The loose syringe with torn wrapper needs to go in the waste
The sealed vacuum tubes need to go in the waste
The clean tray itself needs to go in the waste
trial.explain: Only sealed, first-time needles and syringes can be used for a draw.

episodes.title: First Vein Draw
episodes.text: You sit down beside your first patient with the requisition in hand. You tie the tourniquet and see a thin vein in the arm. You pick up your supplies to begin the draw.

choice.prompt: The vein is thin and rolls a little. Which method do you use?

options.label: Stay with the vacuum tube
options.outcome: You complete the draw with the vacuum tube. The tube fills slowly and you watch it closely.

options.label: Switch to a butterfly needle
options.outcome: You switch to a small butterfly needle for better control. The draw takes a little longer to set up.

episodes.title: Matching Tubes Again
episodes.text: You sit at the counter with a stack of requisition forms. You match each form to the right specimen tubes, one after another. Same as yesterday, same as tomorrow.

episodes.title: Glucose Screening Talk
episodes.text: You greet the patient here for a glucose screening. You explain the stick will be quick.

chat.text: Is this the glucose screening test?
Yes, she's next for screening — tubes are ready.
Okay, just tell me when to look away.

episodes.title: Full Sharps Box
episodes.text: You go to drop a used needle after a draw. The sharps container is full to the line and the lid will not close safely. You hold the tray steady and keep the needle away from your hands.

choice.prompt: The sharps box is full and you are holding a used needle. What do you do?

options.label: Seal and replace the box per policy
options.outcome: You set the needle down safely and seal the full box. You place a new empty container and dispose of the needle.

options.label: Push the needle in to make room
options.outcome: You force the needle into the full box. The lid still will not close and the needles press back up.

episodes.title: Last Blood Culture
episodes.text: You sit with your last patient of the day. You draw blood for a blood culture test and fill the bottles. You match the labels to the requisition form for the lab.

episodes.title: First Booking Email
episodes.text: You arrive and open your laptop. You sit down and read the overnight requests for rentals. You start a new order for a Saturday photo booth rental.

trial.title: Take a rental order
items: Check availability for that date
Confirm the details back to them
Ask what rental they need
Write down the date and time
trial.explain: You ask what they need first, then check it before you confirm anything.

episodes.title: Questions About Rentals
episodes.text: You sit down with your phone list. A customer calls about what you have open next month.

chat.text: Do you have the open booth free on the 14th?
How does it work once it is set up?
What do we have to do to keep it safe?

episodes.title: Showing How It Works
episodes.text: You meet a customer to go over use and care of the booth. You show how it turns on and off. You explain what not to pull or spill on.

choice.prompt: She wants to move the booth herself during the party. What do you do?

options.label: Tell her to leave it in place
options.outcome: You explain it stays where you set it. She agrees to keep it there for the night.

options.label: Walk her through safe care
options.outcome: You show her what to wipe and what to avoid touching. She writes it down for her helper.

episodes.title: Same Totals Again
episodes.text: You sit down and run charges for merchandise and services. You add the same rental lines you added yesterday. You check the math again and save it.

episodes.title: Payment Will Not Go Through
episodes.text: You are taking final payment for a weekend rental. The card declines twice. The customer is waiting and the date is held.

choice.prompt: The payment will not go through. What do you do now?

options.label: Explain the fee and try another method
options.outcome: You calmly state the amount due and ask for another card. She pays with a second card and you give a receipt.

options.label: Pause and explain the policy
options.outcome: You explain the date is only held once payment clears. She calls her bank and you wait to rerun it.

episodes.title: Closing Out Payments
episodes.text: You sit down and add up today's charges and payments. You match each rental order to its receipt. You file the fees and policy sheets for the day.

episodes.title: Planning Morning Shots
episodes.text: You arrive at the small studio and look through today's notes. You sit down with the camera and think about the images you want. You pick the backdrop, move a chair into place, and check the window light.

episodes.title: Setting Up Tripod
episodes.text: You carry the digital camera and tripod to the corner mark. You fix the camera on the tripod and slide on a filter. You clip on the flash attachment and check that it sits firm.

trial.title: Check the setup
trial.scenario: You look through the viewfinder. The frame is steady on the tripod, but the image looks washed and flat under the ceiling lights.
options: The flash attachment is loose
The filter is still on for outdoor light
The tripod legs are locked
trial.explain: The wrong filter flattens the light, so you remove it before shooting.

episodes.title: Adjusting For Light
episodes.text: You watch how the subject moves by the window. You turn the aperture ring and change the shutter speed for the motion. You turn the focus ring until the face looks sharp.

episodes.title: Moving Files Over
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and plug in the card. You transfer photographs to the computer for editing and archiving. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Flash Stops Working
episodes.text: You set up a reflector for the afternoon portraits. You fire a test shot and the flash gives nothing. You check the attachment and the light stays dead.

choice.prompt: The flash is dead and the subject is waiting. What do you do?

options.label: Switch to the reflector and window light
options.outcome: You angle the reflector and keep shooting with steady daylight.

options.label: Stop and try to fix the flash now
options.outcome: You pause the shoot and check the flash connection and settings.

episodes.title: Placing The Subject
episodes.text: You bring the last subject back to the mark for one more setup.

choice.prompt: The client waits for direction on the final shot. How do you place them?

options.label: Adjust their pose and shift the light
options.outcome: You move their shoulder and angle the light for the effect you want.

options.label: Keep them as they are and shoot
options.outcome: You leave the pose alone and take the final frames as they stand.

chat.text: Do I look straight at the camera?
Should my hands be like this?

episodes.title: First Exam Starts
episodes.text: You arrive and meet a new patient in the treatment room. You sit down and perform the initial exam. You watch how they move and note where it hurts.

trial.title: Spot what matters
trial.scenario: You are doing an initial exam. The patient moves stiffly and winces on one step. You need to decide what to focus on first.
options: The painful movement pattern you just saw
The color of their shoes
What time their next visit is
trial.explain: You focus first on the painful movement to identify the problem.

episodes.title: Talking Through Plan
episodes.text: You sit with the patient to go over what the exam showed.

choice.prompt: The patient wants a clear next step and your colleague is waiting. What do you do?

options.label: Confer together now
options.outcome: You talk it through together and agree on the next steps for the program.

options.label: Delay the talk
options.outcome: You set a time later today to confer and assess the program.

chat.text: Will this treatment actually help me move better?
What are you thinking for the intervention program?
I just want to know what comes next.

episodes.title: Same Exercises Again
episodes.text: You bring out the mats for the morning treatment block. You guide the patient through the same set as yesterday. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Teaching Home Practice
episodes.text: You sit with a patient and their family after the session. You show the home treatment procedure slowly. You watch them try it back.

episodes.title: When Pain Spikes
episodes.text: You are carrying out a treatment program when the patient stops with pain. You stay calm and check how they feel. You need to decide how to change the session.

choice.prompt: The patient is hurting and cannot continue as planned. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and ease up
options.outcome: You stop the movement and switch to a gentler position to ease the pain.

options.label: Keep same intensity
options.outcome: You hold the session and recheck their response before you continue.

options.label: End and reassess
options.outcome: You end the activity early and note their response to review the plan.

episodes.title: Charting The Day
episodes.text: You sit down at the computer at the end of the day. You record prognosis, treatment, response, and progress in each chart. You close the notes and head out.

episodes.title: First Morning Visit
episodes.text: You call in your first patient and sit down across from them. You ask about their cough and listen to their lungs. You order a chest X-ray and blood work to diagnose what is going on.

episodes.title: Sharing Test Results
episodes.text: You sit down with a patient to go over yesterday's lab results.

choice.prompt: The results show low iron. They look worried and ask what this means. How do you explain it?

options.label: Explain slowly and check understanding
options.outcome: You explain the result in plain words and pause. They ask two questions and you answer them before prescribing iron.

options.label: Give the short version and the prescription
options.outcome: You tell them it is low iron and hand over the prescription. They nod and leave with the paper, still quiet.

chat.text: So what did the blood test show?
Is that why I keep feeling tired?
What do I do next?

episodes.title: Typing Morning Notes
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk and open the charts from this morning. You type histories, exam findings, and results into each record. Same boxes as yesterday, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Flu Shot Visit
episodes.text: You greet a patient here for a flu vaccination. You confirm they want it and give the shot in the arm. You note the dose in their record before they leave.

trial.title: Give a vaccination
items: Give the shot in the arm
Write down the dose given
Ask about allergies and past reactions
Explain what the vaccine prevents
trial.explain: You check safety first, then explain, give, and record.

episodes.title: Worsening Blood Pressure
episodes.text: You see a regular patient whose blood pressure is higher than last month. You review their home readings and current medication with them. Their headache and numbers suggest the plan is not working.

choice.prompt: Their pressure is still high on the current dose. Do you adjust treatment now or keep watching?

options.label: Adjust the medication now
options.outcome: You change the dose and explain the new plan. They agree to return in two weeks for a recheck.

options.label: Keep the dose and recheck soon
options.outcome: You keep the same prescription and ask them to track readings daily. You book a close follow-up to review progress.

options.label: Ask a colleague to review with you
options.outcome: You step out and review the chart with another physician. You return together and agree on the next change.

episodes.title: Closing Follow Up Calls
episodes.text: You call two patients you started on new medication last week. You ask about side effects and how they feel day to day. You update their records and decide to keep one plan and change the other.

episodes.title: Morning Exam Room
episodes.text: You arrive in the first exam room and wash your hands. You sit down across from the patient and ask what hurts today. You look, listen, and feel to check their physical condition.

episodes.title: Listening to History
episodes.text: You sit with the next patient to take a full health history.

choice.prompt: The history is vague and has gaps. What do you do next?

options.label: Ask clear follow-up questions about timing and past illness
options.outcome: You get a clearer timeline and write it down for the record.

options.label: Move on with what you have
options.outcome: You leave gaps in the history and they carry into the note.

chat.text: It started about a week ago, mostly in the mornings.
I had something like this last year, but not this bad.
I am not sure what else you need to know.

episodes.title: Same Notes Again
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and type up histories and exam findings. It is the same form as yesterday and will be the same tomorrow. You save each note and open the next chart.

episodes.title: Abnormal Lab Result
episodes.text: You open the morning labs and one result is clearly off normal. You sit still and read it again to be sure. The patient is still waiting down the hall.

choice.prompt: The test shows a real deviation that needs a plan now. What do you decide?

options.label: Make a tentative diagnosis and plan next care steps now
options.outcome: You outline treatment and watch closely for change.

options.label: Wait and recheck later without a plan
options.outcome: The abnormal result sits without action while time passes.

options.label: Ask for a quick review before you act
options.outcome: You pause care briefly until another eye confirms the finding.

episodes.title: Sorting the Plan
episodes.text: You sit with your notes and test results together. You weigh what fits and make a tentative diagnosis. You decide on management and treatment to suggest.

trial.title: Nervous question
trial.says: Does this mean something is really wrong with me?
options: You need to calm down, it is probably nothing.
Based on your exam and test results, here is what we see so far.
I cannot tell you anything until all the paperwork is done.
trial.explain: You answer with what the exam and results actually show.

episodes.title: Prescription Approval
episodes.text: You write up the medication plan you decided on earlier. You bring it to the physician for approval and signature. You record the approved prescription in the patient note.

episodes.title: Marking Pipe Runs
episodes.text: You arrive and pull out your ruler and level. You locate where the pipe run and passage holes go. You mark the positions on the wall and floor.

episodes.title: Shutting Off Water
episodes.text: You walk to the pipe section feeding the work area. You fit your valve key and wrench to the valve. You shut off the water before the next step.

episodes.title: Cutting Pipe Lengths
episodes.text: You sit down with the cut list and a length of pipe. You cut with the saw and clean the ends. You thread and shape it to specification.

trial.title: Get pipe to size
items: Thread the cut end with the pipe threader
Cut the pipe to specification with the saw
Shape the section with the pipe bender
Measure and mark the pipe to specification
trial.explain: You measure first, then cut, thread, and bend to fit.

episodes.title: Tightening Same Fittings
episodes.text: You sit and assemble pipe sections with couplings and bolts. It is the same fittings as yesterday. It will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Laying Underground Pipe
episodes.text: You are in the trench extending the water piping. You line up the next section to connect the fixture. The trench wall starts to crumble near your joint.

choice.prompt: The trench edge is slipping by the joint. What do you do?

options.label: Stop and clear the loose soil first
options.outcome: You stop fitting and clear the soil back. The joint takes longer but stays clean and seated.

options.label: Keep fitting to finish the connection
options.outcome: You push the connection together now. You still have to stop afterward to clear soil from around the pipe.

episodes.title: Steam Valve Shutdown
episodes.text: You hear steam hissing at the pipe section. You grab your valve key and wrench.

choice.prompt: The valve is stiff and steam is still coming. What do you do?

options.label: Close it now with the valve key
options.outcome: You seat the valve closed and the flow stops. Your hands get hot and you check the joint after.

options.label: Ask your colleague to help hold it
options.outcome: You both grip and the valve closes together. The flow stops and you move on to the repair.

chat.text: Pressure is still up on that section. Shut it down now.
Valve is stiff. Want me to hold the wrench with you?
Tell me when flow is fully off.

episodes.title: Raising the Scaffold
episodes.text: You arrive at the house and walk to the side wall. You carry frames and planks into place. You lock the pins and test it with your weight.

episodes.title: Covering Windows and Doors
episodes.text: You pull sheets over the windows and doors. You tape the edges down tight. You spread cover over the sidewalk below.

trial.title: Spot the Gap
trial.scenario: You step back to check the covers. The front windows are taped, the sidewalk sheet is flat, but the side door glass is still bare with plaster buckets nearby.
options: Side door glass needs covering
Front windows need another coat
Sidewalk sheet needs more plaster
trial.explain: Bare glass near the work will catch splash.

episodes.title: Mixing the Plaster
episodes.text: You stand by the mixer with your coworker. The first batch looks a little thin.

choice.prompt: The mix is too thin. What do you tell him?

options.label: Add powder and remix
options.outcome: He adds powder and remixes. The mix thickens and you check it before you use it.

options.label: Start a fresh batch
options.outcome: You both dump the thin batch. He starts over while you clean the mixer.

chat.text: This batch feels watery. Want me to add more powder?
Or should I dump it and start over?

episodes.title: First Coat Up
episodes.text: You load your trowel and work plaster across the wall. You keep the strokes even and overlap each pass. You step back to check the thickness.

episodes.title: Coat Sliding Down
episodes.text: You spray the next section of wall. The stucco sags and starts to slide in one spot. You stop spraying and look at the wet patch.

choice.prompt: The fresh coat is sagging. What do you do?

options.label: Scrape it off and respray
options.outcome: You scrape the sagged spot clean. You respray it thinner and it holds.

options.label: Smooth it with a trowel
options.outcome: You work the sag flat with your trowel. You watch it closely before moving on.

episodes.title: Sweeping Up Again
episodes.text: You pull the covers off the windows and doors. You sweep plaster bits off the sidewalk. You stack the tools the same as yesterday.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Platform Engineer — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Marking Pipe Runs
episodes.text: You arrive with your ruler and level. You measure and mark where the pipes, connections, and fixtures will go. You check each passage hole mark twice before anything is cut.

trial.title: Check the Marks
trial.scenario: You hold the ruler and level to your marks. Three fixture marks sit level on the pipe line, but one passage hole mark is crooked and off the line.
options: The crooked passage hole mark
A level fixture mark
The ruler itself
trial.explain: You fix the off-line mark first so the pipe and holes line up.

episodes.title: Shutting Off Water
episodes.text: You turn the valve key and shut off the water to the pipe section. You check with the wrench that the valve is fully closed. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Cutting Pipe to Size
episodes.text: You measure the pipe and cut it with the saw. You thread the end with the pipe threader to spec. You bend one section with the bender where it needs to turn.

episodes.title: Laying Underground Pipe
episodes.text: You work in the trench extending the water piping to connect the fixtures. You set the next length of sanitary pipe in place. The end sits a little short of the connection.

choice.prompt: The pipe end sits short of the fixture connection. What do you do?

options.label: Extend with another short length
options.outcome: You cut and fit a short extension and cement the joint. The line reaches the fixture and holds.

options.label: Shift the whole run forward
options.outcome: You loosen the couplings and slide the run forward. You re-check the joints to make sure they still seat.

episodes.title: Stopping a Leak Fast
episodes.text: Water is spraying from a pipe section and pooling fast. You grab your valve key and wrench and reach the shutoff valve. You need to stop the flow before repair.

choice.prompt: The valve is stiff and water is still pushing through. What do you do?

options.label: Close it fully with the wrench
options.outcome: You seat the wrench and turn the valve fully closed. The spray drops and the section drains.

options.label: Close the next upstream valve
options.outcome: You leave this valve and close the next valve up the line. The water to this section stops.

episodes.title: Joining Pipe Sections
episodes.text: You sit with pipe sections, couplings, and clamps. You assemble the fittings with plastic solvent and screws. You tighten each bolt and check the joints.

episodes.title: Checking Today's Topic
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down with yesterday's notes. You search the internet and click through video archives for background. You pull together what you need on the production topic.

episodes.title: Planning Each Shot
episodes.text: You sit with the plan for the next scene. You work out the framing, composition, and camera movement. You note the sound and where each person moves.

choice.prompt: The small movement does not fit the framing you planned. Do you keep it or change the plan?

options.label: Change the camera movement to fit
options.outcome: You redraw the movement on the plan. The shot now fits and the crew uses the new version.

options.label: Keep the framing and cut the movement
options.outcome: You cross the movement off the plan. The shot stays simple and matches the framing.

episodes.title: Talking Through The Scene
episodes.text: You stand with the actors before the take. You explain the approach and characterization for the scene. You walk them through where to move and when.

episodes.title: Reviewing The Take
episodes.text: You sit down and play back the recording. You watch and listen against production and broadcast standards. You mark the parts that do not match.

trial.title: Find what fails first
trial.scenario: You review the recording to check conformance to production and broadcast standards. The framing and camera movement match the plan, but the sound cuts out for a few seconds.
options: The sound dropout in the middle section
The framing that matches the plan
The camera movement that matches the plan
trial.explain: Sound must meet standards, so the dropout is the part to fix first.

episodes.title: Live Recording Trouble
episodes.text: You are directing the live recording.

choice.prompt: You are directing live and the scene drifts from the plan. What do you do now?

options.label: Stop and redo the scene to standard
options.outcome: You cut the live take and direct it again. The recording restarts and runs a few minutes late.

options.label: Keep directing and keep it live
options.outcome: You keep directing through the scene. The flaw stays in the recording and you note it for review.

chat.text: We are live in one minute. The next scene is not matching the standard.
Tell me what you want to do.

episodes.title: Same Check Again
episodes.text: You sit down with the day's recordings. You play them through again for production and broadcast standards. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: First Foot Check
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down with your first patient. You ask about the pain and past foot problems. You examine the foot and pull up the x-ray on the screen.

choice.prompt: The exam and x-ray point to a joint problem, but you are not fully sure. What do you do next?

options.label: Order a lab test to confirm
options.outcome: You order the lab test and ask the patient to wait for results before you decide on treatment.

options.label: Make the diagnosis from what you have
options.outcome: You explain your diagnosis from the history, exam, and x-ray and move on to treatment options.

episodes.title: Showing Foot Care
episodes.text: You sit with a patient whose bunion is settling down. You show how to wash, dry, and check the feet each day. You talk through what to watch for to prevent future problems.

trial.title: What do you say
trial.says: How do I stop this from coming back?
options: Just hope it stays better on its own.
Here is how to care for your feet each day to prevent future problems.
You should stop walking on that foot completely.
trial.explain: You advise the patient about foot care techniques needed to prevent future problems.

episodes.title: Same Checks Again
episodes.text: You work through routine ankle and foot checks. You test the same joints and write the same notes. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Removing Ingrown Nail
episodes.text: You set up for a small surgery on an ingrown nail. You numb the toe and remove the ingrown edge. You clean the area and cover it.

episodes.title: Swollen Painful Abscess
episodes.text: A patient comes in with a hot, swollen foot abscess that needs quick care.

choice.prompt: The abscess looks ready to drain and the patient is in pain. What do you do?

options.label: Treat it surgically now
options.outcome: You numb the area and surgically drain the abscess and arrange follow-up care.

options.label: Prescribe medication and watch it
options.outcome: You prescribe medication, explain warning signs, and ask the patient to return if it worsens.

chat.text: It got much worse overnight. It really hurts to stand.
Can you do something today?

episodes.title: Writing Prescriptions Out
episodes.text: You sit down to finish the day's orders. You write out medications and a corrective device order. You add a referral for physical therapy.

episodes.title: Morning Briefing Begins
episodes.text: You arrive for shift and sit down for briefing. You hear about overnight calls and your patrol area. You head out to maintain order and protect people and property.

episodes.title: Talking With Neighbors
episodes.text: You walk the block and stop to talk with residents. You listen to concerns about late-night foot traffic.

choice.prompt: They ask you to stop by more at night. What do you do?

options.label: Say you will add it to patrols
options.outcome: You tell them you will drive through after dark. They thank you and head back inside.

options.label: Ask what times they hear it
options.outcome: You write down the times they give you. You say you will share it with the next shift.

chat.text: We hear a lot of noise by the alley at night.
Can you come by more often after dark?

episodes.title: Driving The Same Route
episodes.text: You drive the same streets checking speed and parking. You watch traffic and enforce motor vehicle laws. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Crash At Intersection
episodes.text: You respond to a two-car crash at an intersection. You park to block traffic and check both drivers. One person is bleeding from the arm and needs first aid.

choice.prompt: One driver is hurt and traffic is building. What do you do first?

options.label: Render first aid to the injured driver
options.outcome: You press cloth to the cut and stay with them until medics arrive. Traffic waits while you help.

options.label: Direct traffic around the cars first
options.outcome: You wave cars past the crash, then return to check the injury. The hurt driver waits a few minutes for aid.

options.label: Call for backup and medics, then help
options.outcome: You radio for medics and backup, then start first aid. Help arrives while you stay with the driver.

episodes.title: Reviewing What Happened
episodes.text: You sit down with notes from a store dispute this morning. You review the facts to see if a criminal act was involved. You compare what you saw with statute violations.

trial.title: Find The Possible Violation
trial.scenario: You review notes from a dispute at a store. One person pushed the other and an item broke. You check which fact points to a possible criminal act.
options: The push that may be assault
The loud voices alone
The store's closing time
trial.explain: The physical push is the fact that may show a violation.

episodes.title: Writing The Reports
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and open your notebook. You record the facts from today's incidents and activities. You prepare reports that document what happened.

episodes.title: Morning Checks Again
episodes.text: You arrive at the first backyard pool. You check fluid levels and look over the motors and belts. You swap the skimmer filter just like yesterday. You write the readings down and head to the van.

episodes.title: Noisy Pump Check
episodes.text: You get to the second house and the pump rattles loudly. You turn it on and off and listen to the motor. You watch the drive shake when it runs.

choice.prompt: The pump still rattles when you test it. Do you keep running it or shut it off to inspect?

options.label: Shut it off and inspect
options.outcome: You shut off the power and find a loose belt. You can see the problem clearly now.

options.label: Run one more test
options.outcome: You run it for a few seconds and hear the rattle get worse. You shut it off to avoid more damage.

episodes.title: Leveling The Pump
episodes.text: You sit down by the pump pad with your hand tools. You loosen the mounts and shift the motor straight. You check it with your level and tighten it back down.

trial.title: Spot The Problem
trial.scenario: You operate the pump to test it. The motor hums steady and the drive belt looks tight. The filter gauge reads high and the water flow stays weak.
options: Filter needs replacing
Motor needs replacing
Belt needs tightening
trial.explain: High gauge pressure with weak flow means the filter is clogged.

episodes.title: Motor Stops Fast
episodes.text: You are at the community pool when the main motor dies. The water goes still in the midday heat.

choice.prompt: The motor will not restart and swimmers are coming soon. What do you do?

options.label: Make a temporary repair now
options.outcome: You reset the connections and tighten parts with your wrenches. The pump runs for the afternoon while you plan a full fix.

options.label: Keep it off and close the pool
options.outcome: You lock out the equipment and tell them to keep people out. The water sits still until the proper repair is done.

chat.text: The pump just quit. Is the pool okay?
We have swimmers coming at 2. Can you fix it?
Just tell me what you need.

episodes.title: Ordering New Filter
episodes.text: You sit in the van with the supplier catalog. You look up the filter size and belt number from today. You call in the order for parts and supplies.

episodes.title: Fixing The Seal
episodes.text: You are back at the last house with your tools. You pull the worn seal and fit the new one. You run the pump with your test meter and watch it hold steady.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Power Plant Operator — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Opening The Dashboards
episodes.text: You arrive and open your laptop at your desk. You pull up yesterday's visits, clicks, and cost per click. You drink coffee while the numbers load.

episodes.title: Rewriting A Tired Ad
episodes.text: You sit down with one search ad that stopped getting clicks. You look at what people typed to find it. You rewrite the text to match those words more closely.

episodes.title: Same Numbers Again
episodes.text: You copy visits, page views, and time on site into the same sheet. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow. You save it and close the tab.

episodes.title: Planning With Marketing
episodes.text: You join a short call about next month's online marketing plan.

choice.prompt: The team needs your call on where to place the extra keywords.

options.label: Put them on mobile placements
options.outcome: You move the keywords to mobile. The team updates the plan and watches mobile clicks this week.

options.label: Keep them on desktop search
options.outcome: You keep the keywords on desktop. The team leaves the plan as is and checks desktop conversions next week.

chat.text: We can push one keyword group harder. Where should we put it?
Search patterns point to mobile or desktop right now?

episodes.title: Fixing Mobile Display
episodes.text: You open a landing page on your phone. The headline runs long and the image loads slow. You shorten the text and resize the image so it reads clean.

trial.title: Order the metrics check
items: Check click-through rates and conversion rates
Note visits and time on site
Compare cost per click and cost per acquisition
Pull transaction volume and revenue
trial.explain: You start with visits, then clicks, then sales, then costs.

episodes.title: Tracking Goes Dark
episodes.text: You see conversions stopped tracking this afternoon. Marketing needs the report tomorrow. You have to decide what to do now.

choice.prompt: Tracking is broken and the report is due. What do you do first?

options.label: Pause the affected ads until tracking is fixed
options.outcome: You pause those ads. Spend stops while you flag the tracking gap for the report.

options.label: Keep ads running and note the gap
options.outcome: You keep the ads running. You mark today's conversions as missing in tomorrow's report.

options.label: Fix the tracking tag now
options.outcome: You check the tag and fix it. Today's earlier clicks stay untracked while new data comes in.

episodes.title: Morning Media Request
episodes.text: You arrive and open your inbox. A reporter has asked for background on yesterday's announcement. You read the request and check who should answer it.

choice.prompt: The reporter needs an answer by noon. Do you respond yourself or pass it on?

options.label: Answer it yourself
options.outcome: You send a short factual reply and copy the reporter on the source document.

options.label: Designate a spokesperson
options.outcome: You forward the request to the right manager and tell the reporter who will call back.

episodes.title: Drafting the Release
episodes.text: You sit down to write a press release for a client. You keep the facts in order and keep the language simple. You read it back once for errors.

trial.title: Check the draft
trial.scenario: You have a draft press release to promote a client event. The date is right and the quotes are approved, but the contact name at the bottom is from an old release.
options: Fix the media contact name first
Add another quote
Change the headline font
trial.explain: The release cannot work if reporters cannot reach the right contact.

episodes.title: Updating the Feeds
episodes.text: You log in to the company site and social accounts. You post the scheduled update and fix one old link. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Community Group Call
episodes.text: You call a neighborhood group to keep the relationship steady. You listen more than you talk.

chat.text: We had questions about the parking lot plan last night.
Can someone come explain it next week?
Noted, I will bring dates for that meeting.

episodes.title: Urgent Reporter Deadline
episodes.text: A second reporter calls with a tight deadline and a sharp question. You do not have all the facts yet. You need to decide what to say right now.

choice.prompt: The reporter is waiting on the line. What do you do?

options.label: Give what you know and follow up
options.outcome: You share only confirmed facts and promise the missing detail by email today.

options.label: Name a spokesperson to speak
options.outcome: You explain you will have the right person call back within the hour.

options.label: Ask for more time
options.outcome: The reporter agrees to wait until 5 PM and you start gathering answers.

episodes.title: Planning Next Message
episodes.text: You sit with your notes and outline next week's program update. You list what the organization did and what is next. You file the plan for review.

episodes.title: Morning Circle Rules
episodes.text: You open the door and greet each child by name. You sit them down on the rug in a circle. You go over the room rules for listening and taking turns.

episodes.title: Learning Colors Together
episodes.text: You sit down at the small table with crayons and shape cards. You ask the children to name the colors and shapes out loud. One girl stays quiet and looks away.

choice.prompt: She will not name a color. What do you do now?

options.label: Offer her a different material to try
options.outcome: She points to red blocks instead of the card and says the color. You stay with her a minute longer.

options.label: Keep asking her with the same card
options.outcome: She shakes her head and slides back in her chair. You move the lesson along to the others.

options.label: Let her watch while others answer
options.outcome: She watches the others and later repeats a color softly. You nod and keep the table calm.

episodes.title: Washing Hands Again
episodes.text: You line the children up at the sink. You watch each one soap, rinse, and dry their hands. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Pouring Milk Carefully
episodes.text: You seat the children at the tables for snack. You serve milk and apple slices in the right portions. You stay nearby while they eat.

trial.title: Serve snack in order
items: You wipe the tables clean after eating
You hand out the cups of milk and apple slices
You seat the children at the tables
You check the portion chart on the wall
trial.explain: You check portions first, then seat, serve, and clean.

episodes.title: Two Hands One Toy
episodes.text: You see two boys tugging on the same truck in the corner. Their voices are getting louder.

choice.prompt: Both boys are pulling and upset. What do you do now?

options.label: Step between them and restate the rule
options.outcome: You remind them we take turns and set a timer. They let go and wait for their turns.

options.label: Take the truck away for now
options.outcome: You put the truck on the shelf and guide them to other toys. They cry a little, then settle.

chat.text: Those two are at it again over the truck.
Can you step in? I am stuck at the paint table.

episodes.title: Afternoon Play Choices
episodes.text: You lay out blocks, dress-up clothes, and drawing paper. You watch what each child picks up and joins. You swap a puzzle for cars for the boy who loves wheels.

episodes.title: Emptying Morning Trash
episodes.text: You arrive with your keys and start at the back bins. You pull each liner, tie it off, and wheel them to the dumpster. You put fresh liners in before anyone walks in.

episodes.title: Sweeping the Floors
episodes.text: You sweep the hallway end to end, then mop the same stretch. You pass the same doors and the same dust as yesterday. You finish one floor and start the next one the same way.

episodes.title: Checking the Restrooms
episodes.text: You step into the upstairs restroom to clean and restock it. A customer waits by the door and speaks up.

choice.prompt: She needs to use the restroom while you are mid-clean. What do you do?

options.label: Pause cleaning and let her use it
options.outcome: You step out and let her in. You wait by your cart and finish wiping and restocking after she leaves.

options.label: Ask her to wait two minutes
options.outcome: You finish wiping the sink and putting out paper, then wave her in. The restroom is fully clean when she enters.

chat.text: Hi, is this restroom open right now?
I can wait if you need a few minutes to finish cleaning.

episodes.title: Scrubbing the Lobby
episodes.text: You get down with the scrub brush for the lobby tile. You work the corners in slow circles and wipe up the gray water. The line between clean and still-dirty shows sharp.

trial.title: Put floor cleaning in order
items: Mop the section and let it dry
Sweep up loose dirt and dust
Fill the mop bucket with clean water
Empty the dirty water and rinse tools
trial.explain: You clear the loose dirt first so the mop water stays clean.

episodes.title: Burning Smell Upstairs
episodes.text: You walk the second floor checking plugs and appliances for safety. You smell hot plastic near the break room outlet and see a brown mark. The coffee maker cord feels hot to touch.

choice.prompt: The outlet is hot and marked brown. What do you do first?

options.label: Unplug the coffee maker
options.outcome: You pull the plug and leave the outlet alone. The smell fades and you tell the manager it needs a repair.

options.label: Leave it plugged in and keep cleaning
options.outcome: You keep working and check back in ten minutes. The mark looks darker and the room still smells hot.

episodes.title: Locking Up Downstairs
episodes.text: You walk the building to lock the doors after hours. You pull each door handle and glance into each empty room. You switch off the hall lights as you head out.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Print-on-Demand Seller — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block

episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Checking Morning Delivery
episodes.text: You arrive early and meet the delivery at the back door. You open each box and check the produce and dairy. You set aside a soft box of greens that does not meet your standard.

episodes.title: Same Kitchen Check
episodes.text: You walk the small kitchen with the same checklist as yesterday. You look over the counters, boards, and fridge handles. You wipe one spot and mark it down.

episodes.title: Showing New Garnish
episodes.text: You stand beside the helper at the cutting board. You show the garnish cut once, slowly.

choice.prompt: The helper's cut is too thick. What do you do right now?

options.label: Show the cut again and watch them try
options.outcome: You take the knife and show the cut again. They copy you and the next pile looks right.

options.label: Move them to washing and finish it yourself
options.outcome: You send them to wash lettuce and finish the garnish yourself. The plate goes out right but you are behind.

chat.text: Chef, is this thin enough like you showed?
I do not want to cut it wrong again.

episodes.title: Guiding Lunch Prep
episodes.text: You stand at the stove while both helpers work their stations. You call out the order and keep the timing together. You check each pan before the plates go up.

trial.title: Put the dish in order
items: Cook the food
Present the food
Prepare the ingredients
Garnish the plate
trial.explain: You prepare first, then cook, then garnish, then present.

episodes.title: Catching Missed Wash
episodes.text: You see a helper move from the trash straight back to the board. They did not wash their hands or change gloves. You step in and stop the line for a moment.

choice.prompt: The food is on the board and hands were not washed. What do you do?

options.label: Stop, throw the touched food and have them wash
options.outcome: You throw the touched food, they wash and reglove. You start that small batch over.

options.label: Have them wash now and keep working
options.outcome: They wash and come back quickly. You keep the line moving but watch them closely.

options.label: Pull them aside for full sanitation review
options.outcome: You pause their station and walk through the washing steps again. Service slows for a few minutes.

episodes.title: Ordering Tomorrow Supplies
episodes.text: You sit down with the stock list at the table. You count what is left in the fridge and pantry. You write the order for food and supplies for tomorrow.

episodes.title: Morning Case Notes
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open yesterday's file. You sit down and type up what you saw and heard. You save the case summary for the record.

episodes.title: Searching Public Records
episodes.text: You sit at your computer and start a paid search for a missing person. You check databases, credit reports, and public records. You pull tax and legal filings to compile what you find.

trial.title: Put the search in order
items: Compile the findings into a summary for the file
Open the database and enter the subject's name
Check credit reports and public records linked to the name
Note any matching tax or legal filings
trial.explain: You start with the name, check records, then compile the results.

episodes.title: Background Check Call
episodes.text: You meet with an employer who paid for a pre-employment check. You walk through the person's character, finances, and history.

choice.prompt: The employer asks for details beyond the background report. What do you share?

options.label: Share only what the check verified
options.outcome: You read back the verified work history and financial facts. The employer thanks you and ends the meeting.

options.label: Add your personal guess about him
options.outcome: You catch yourself and return to the documented findings. You note the employer wants a clean written copy.

chat.text: Did anything come up on his work history?
What about the financial part of the check?

episodes.title: Same Database Checks
episodes.text: You sit back down and run the same database searches as yesterday. You scroll through public records and filings line by line. You log the same kinds of results again.

episodes.title: Questionable Injury Claim
episodes.text: You look at a paid insurance case where the claim does not match the records. You compare the filed claim to the activity you documented. You see signs the claim may be fraudulent.

choice.prompt: You see evidence the funds claimed do not fit the facts. What do you do next?

options.label: Flag it and document the mismatch
options.outcome: You write down the dates, records, and what does not match. You send the file on for review.

options.label: Ignore it and close the file
options.outcome: You leave the mismatch in your notes and move on. The file stays open until you document it.

options.label: Confront the claimant yourself
options.outcome: You hold off and keep to documenting what you found. You add the new details to the case summary.

episodes.title: Evening Paid Follow-Up
episodes.text: You drive out to finish a paid investigation you started last week. You watch, take notes, and check what you see against the file. You head back to write it all down.

episodes.title: Morning Kitchen Table
episodes.text: You arrive at the first house and sit down at the kitchen table. You work one-on-one with the student on yesterday's math problems. You walk through each solution together until it makes sense.

episodes.title: Low Confidence
episodes.text: You sit with a student who keeps saying she gets it wrong.

choice.prompt: She looks down and stops talking. How do you give feedback right now?

options.label: Point out what she did right on the last work
options.outcome: She nods and tries the next problem. She still works slowly but keeps going.

options.label: Move on quickly to the next hard problem
options.outcome: She stays quiet and guesses. You spend the next minutes re-explaining the steps.

chat.text: I'm just bad at this. I always mess up.
You did get the last two right. What helped there?

episodes.title: Same Worksheets Again
episodes.text: You sit down with the same worksheets as yesterday. You review the same pages and the same kinds of problems. You check answers the same way. Tomorrow will be the same.

episodes.title: Showing How to Study
episodes.text: You sit with a student and open his notebook. You show him how to take short notes while he reads. You practice a simple way to plan time on tests.

trial.title: Encouraging effort
trial.says: I studied for an hour and still failed the quiz.
options: You wasted your time if you still failed.
You kept at it for a full hour, and that effort counts. Let's look at what to change.
You are probably just not good at tests.
trial.explain: Positive feedback names the effort and points to the next step.

episodes.title: Stuck Before Test
episodes.text: You sit with a student the day before his test. He freezes on the review problems and cannot finish them. You see his progress has slipped back.

choice.prompt: The test is tomorrow and he is stuck. What do you do now?

options.label: Stop and review the basic steps together
options.outcome: He calms down and works through two easy problems. You cover less material but he finishes something.

options.label: Keep pushing through the test review
options.outcome: He guesses at most answers and gets frustrated. You note what he missed for next time.

options.label: End the practice early and plan study steps
options.outcome: He packs up and listens to your study plan. He leaves with clear pages to review tonight.

episodes.title: Checking Today's Progress
episodes.text: You sit with your last student and look over today's work. You compare it to where he started this morning. You tell him what improved and what still needs work.

episodes.title: Opening Case Folders
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and pull out today's case folders. You check each one for the contract terms and last visit notes. You add the new pages where they belong.

trial.title: Missing Check Note
trial.scenario: You flip through a folder before a meeting. The probation contract is filed inside. The last curfew check note is not there. The background notes are there.
options: The missing curfew check note
The probation contract
The background notes
trial.explain: The missing note leaves the supervision record incomplete.

episodes.title: Morning Check In
episodes.text: You sit down with a man on probation for his regular meeting. You ask about work and his curfew hours.

chat.text: I made all my curfews this week.
Work is steady, four shifts.
I am still behind on my class fee.

episodes.title: Talking Through Anger
episodes.text: You meet with a probationer to talk about how drinking and anger played a part in his offense. You listen and keep the talk steady. You link it back to the terms in his rehabilitation plan.

choice.prompt: He goes quiet when you ask about drinking last weekend. What do you do next?

options.label: Ask him directly about it
options.outcome: He admits he drank on Saturday. You note it in his progress and review the plan terms together.

options.label: Move on to work and school
options.outcome: He relaxes and talks about his job. You circle back to drinking later in the meeting.

episodes.title: Filing The Same Forms
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk and file check sheets into folders. You copy dates and times into the log. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Calling Family Background
episodes.text: You call an offender's sister to gather background information for the file. You ask about home life and daily routine. You write down what she tells you.

episodes.title: Missed Curfew Check
episodes.text: You drive out for a curfew check on home detention. The door stays shut and the lights are off.

choice.prompt: No one answers at the door during curfew hours. What do you do next?

options.label: Wait and knock again
options.outcome: He opens the door after a few minutes. You check who is home and log the late answer.

options.label: Call him and document the check
options.outcome: He answers and says he will come to the door. You record the time and what happened.

options.label: Leave and note no contact
options.outcome: You drive to the next address. You write no contact in the folder for follow-up.

chat.text: Sorry, my phone died.
I am at home now.

episodes.title: Morning Market Review
episodes.text: You log on and open last quarter's sales and cost notes. You compare them against the team's objectives for the online store. You mark which parts of the marketing strategy are working and which are not.

episodes.title: Call With Promotions
episodes.text: You join a video call with the advertising manager to plan next week's promotion. She shares two ideas for pushing the new bundle.

choice.prompt: Which promotion direction do you pick with the advertising manager?

options.label: Discount the bundle for three days
options.outcome: You approve the short discount and she sets up the pricing banner. You watch orders for three days to see if it lifts sales.

options.label: Feature the bundle on the homepage
options.outcome: You approve the homepage spot and she builds the feature block. You leave the price as is and check clicks at the end of the week.

chat.text: I have two options to promote the new bundle this week.
We can discount it for three days, or feature it on the homepage.
Which direction should we go with?

episodes.title: Updating Product List
episodes.text: You sit down to update the list describing product offerings. You check each name and description line by line. It is the same list as yesterday, and it will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Working On Pricing
episodes.text: You open the pricing sheet for two online plans. You weigh what the firm needs against what customers will pay. You draft a small price change to test the balance.

trial.title: Spot the Pricing Problem
trial.scenario: You review a draft price that covers costs and meets firm goals. Early notes show customers find it too high for the value, and satisfaction is dropping.
options: The price hurts customer satisfaction
The product list has a typo
The ad colors are wrong
trial.explain: Pricing has to balance firm goals with customer satisfaction.

episodes.title: Budget Warning Flag
episodes.text: You open the product development budget and see expenditures running past the projection. The return-on-investment no longer looks safe for this quarter. You need to decide what to pause before you spend more.

choice.prompt: The numbers are over budget. What do you pull back first?

options.label: Pause extra development spending
options.outcome: You freeze the extra development spend and update the budget sheet. The projection steadies but the next feature ships later.

options.label: Pause extra promotion spending
options.outcome: You cut the extra promotion spend and update the expenditure log. The budget steadies but fewer new customers see the product.

episodes.title: Writing Cost Summary
episodes.text: You sit down to record budgets, expenditures, and profit-loss projections. You fill in each line for product development this month. You save the file for the finance review.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Project Manager — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Opening The Property Office
episodes.text: You arrive and unlock the management office. You check overnight messages about maintenance and operations. You list what needs attention first today.

episodes.title: Talking Through Late Rent
episodes.text: You sit down with a tenant who missed the monthly rent payment. You open the rent ledger on your desk.

choice.prompt: You need to direct collection of the rent due now. What do you do?

options.label: Take half now and set a written date for the rest
options.outcome: You take the partial payment and write down the balance due date. You file the receipt and check it again next week.

options.label: Ask for the full payment today
options.outcome: You explain the full amount is due and wait while they try to pay. You log whatever is paid and note what is still owed.

chat.text: I can pay half today and the rest next week.
Will that keep me clear for this month?

episodes.title: Logging The Same Payments
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and log rental fees and deposits in the same spreadsheet as yesterday. You match each payment to its unit. Same entries tomorrow.

episodes.title: Planning The Hallway Repair
episodes.text: You walk the second-floor hallway to look at peeling paint and a loose light. You call the maintenance worker to line up the fix. You post a note for residents about the work time.

trial.title: Order the repair steps
items: Call the maintenance worker to schedule the repair date
Walk the hallway to confirm what repair is needed
Tell residents when the work will happen
Check the finished work and close it out
trial.explain: You look first, then schedule, then tell residents, then check the work.

episodes.title: Burst Pipe Downstairs
episodes.text: You get a call about water leaking in a ground-floor unit. You hurry down and see water spreading from under the sink. You shut off the valve and call for a major repair.

choice.prompt: Water is still on the floor and more units could be affected. What do you handle first?

options.label: Stop the water and move items out of the way
options.outcome: You keep the water off and help move boxes and rugs clear. The plumber arrives to start the repair.

options.label: Call upstairs tenants to check for leaks
options.outcome: You knock upstairs and find a second leak starting. You shut that valve too and add it to the repair call.

episodes.title: Budget And Rent Review
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk and open the property budget. You compare current rents with nearby listings. You update the monthly financial report with expenses and payments.

episodes.title: Morning Charts Review
episodes.text: You arrive and open the same patient files as yesterday. You check social and medical history notes for updates. You save each file the same way you always do.

episodes.title: Morning Health Check
episodes.text: You sit down with a new patient in the exam room. You ask about sleep, mood, and physical health. You order a basic lab test to check general condition.

episodes.title: Team Care Talk
episodes.text: You join the psychologist and social worker to go over treatment progress.

choice.prompt: The team waits on your call about his treatment plan. What do you do?

options.label: Stay with the current plan
options.outcome: You keep the plan and ask the team to watch his sleep for another week.

options.label: Adjust the plan together
options.outcome: You agree on a small change and each person writes down their next step.

chat.text: His sleep is still poor after two weeks on this plan.
Do you want to keep the same approach or change it?
Let us know your call so we can update our notes.

episodes.title: Setting The Treatment
episodes.text: You sit with a patient to set an individual care plan. You talk through medication and talk therapy options. You prescribe the medication you both agree on.

trial.title: What Comes First
trial.scenario: You review a patient file before prescribing. The social history is missing. The last lab result shows a physical issue you have not addressed.
options: Deal with the physical issue shown in the lab result first
Rewrite the old social history notes
File the chart and move on
trial.explain: Physical health information must be addressed before prescribing safely.

episodes.title: Urgent Patient Help
episodes.text: You are called in when a patient becomes deeply distressed. You sit close and check his current state. You decide on a psychotherapeutic treatment to give now.

choice.prompt: He is getting worse and you must act now. What do you do?

options.label: Give a calming treatment now
options.outcome: You administer the treatment and stay with him until he settles.

options.label: Pause and gather more history first
options.outcome: You step out to call his relative for history while a nurse stays with him.

options.label: Ask for another clinician to step in
options.outcome: You hand over the immediate care and brief the clinician on what you saw.

episodes.title: Evening Notes Update
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and open today's patient records. You add the new histories and treatment notes. You close each file so tomorrow starts clear.

episodes.title: First Client Sits
episodes.text: You arrive and set your chairs straight. You sit down across from your first client. You listen while they talk through what brought them in.

episodes.title: Listening For Patterns
episodes.text: You sit with a new client and ask about sleep, mood, and history. You look back at their intake forms and test notes. You start to name what might be going on.

episodes.title: Checking For Safety
episodes.text: A client tells you they have been thinking about hurting themselves. You stay calm and start your risk questions.

choice.prompt: They won't promise to stay safe tonight. What do you do next?

options.label: Stay and complete a full safety plan
options.outcome: You walk through warning signs and contacts together. You agree on who they will call if things get worse.

options.label: Arrange urgent support right away
options.outcome: You call for backup and stay with them until help arrives. The morning runs late but they are not left alone.

chat.text: I don't think I can keep myself safe tonight.
Stay with them. Walk through the safety check now.

episodes.title: Same Notes Again
episodes.text: You sit at your desk after lunch. You type up session notes and progress notes. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Family Around Table
episodes.text: You bring a family into the room and let each person speak. Tension rises when goals come up. You help them keep it plain and workable.

choice.prompt: The parents disagree loudly about the next step. How do you step in?

options.label: Pause and restate each goal
options.outcome: You repeat back what each person said in simple words. The room quiets enough to pick one small next step.

options.label: Set one shared action plan
options.outcome: You write down one clear plan they can all try this week. They leave with the same page in hand.

options.label: Meet with the teen alone
options.outcome: You ask the parents to wait outside for ten minutes. You hear the teen's side without interruption.

episodes.title: Reports Before Home
episodes.text: You close your door and open your files. You write up reports on today's clients. You file each treatment plan where it belongs.

trial.title: File the Note
items: Update the treatment plan
Write the session notes
Add recommendations
Record progress notes
trial.explain: You record what happened before you plan what happens next.

episodes.title: First Exercise Set
episodes.text: You arrive on the gym floor and greet your first patient. You walk them through their leg lifts rep by rep. You stay close, count with them, and keep their form safe.

episodes.title: Encouraging Tired Legs
episodes.text: You sit down beside a patient who is slowing down halfway through standing exercises. You watch their breathing and how they shift their weight. You keep your voice steady and remind them to rest a hand on the rail.

choice.prompt: She says she is tired and wants to quit the last set. What do you do?

options.label: Offer a short rest then try together
options.outcome: She rests a minute, then finishes three more reps with your help. You note she needed a break but completed the set.

options.label: End the set and move to seated rest
options.outcome: She sits down and catches her breath. You note she stopped early and will tell the physical therapist.

episodes.title: Straps and Seats Again
episodes.text: You secure the next patient onto the therapy bike. You tighten the straps and check the seat. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Pool Steps Practice
episodes.text: You bring a patient to the small therapy pool to work on walking. You show the slow step on deck before you get in. You stay at their side in the water while they practice.

trial.title: Order the pool steps
items: Walk with them for a few steps in the water
Show the step on deck first
Help them down the pool steps
Ask how the movement felt
trial.explain: You show the movement first, then enter safely before you practice and check in.

episodes.title: Wobble On Mat
episodes.text: You are guarding a patient during standing balance work when his knees buckle.

choice.prompt: He is unsteady and asking to sit. What do you do now?

options.label: Steady him and help him sit at once
options.outcome: You hold his gait belt and guide him to the mat to sit. You check how he feels and watch him until he steadies.

options.label: Have him try one more rep standing
options.outcome: You keep holding him while he tries another step. He sways more, so you help him sit and end the activity.

options.label: Call for the physical therapist
options.outcome: You help him sit safely and ask the physical therapist to come over. You share what you saw with his balance and dizziness.

chat.text: Whoa, I feel dizzy.
My legs just gave out a bit.
Can I sit down?

episodes.title: Notes Before Home
episodes.text: You sit down at the desk with your patient list. You write short notes on exercises, help given, and how each person responded. You send the progress notes to the physical therapist.
